Its unauthorized retry change is narrower than B’s global buffering of arbitrary reader bodies.","reasons":["Both patches add the required Upload signature, use multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", validate inputs, and produce a replayable multipart body.","Both violate the explicit requirement to route Upload through FilesService.Add, instead duplicating its option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error.","B broadly changes RawClient.Do to io.ReadAll every non-native reader unless WithNoRetry is set. That introduces unbounded buffering and changes streaming behavior across RawClient, Files.Add, Files.Update, and unrelated APIs.","A limits its extra RawClient behavior to io.ReadSeeker values and preserves one-shot streaming for forward-only readers, making its scope violation materially narrower than B’s expansion despite still being unauthorized by the contract terms clearly mentioned in the frozen contract regarding no changes to unrelated retry machinery or Add behavior; both candidates violated that. Candidate A does make raw handling more complex than necessary, but less globally disruptive overall. Candidate B has stronger explicit coverage of source-reader errors and FilesOption propagation, while A has the stronger Upload retry test: it uses an actual open file and verifies identical multipart bodies across attempts."],"risks_a":["Its GetBody closure returns wrappers around the same mutable io.ReadSeeker rather than independent body copies, which is fragile for redirects or concurrent replay.","It changes reader ownership and Files.Add behavior through RawClient.Do, contrary to the contract.","Upload duplicates Files.Add instead of delegating to it, and there is no Upload source-reader failure test."],"risks_b":["Generic io.ReadAll buffering can consume excessive memory or block indefinitely on pipes and long-lived streams.","It changes read timing, source-reader position and closure behavior, and retry semantics for every non-native reader in RawClient.Do.","Upload duplicates Files.Add instead of delegating to it; its retry test counts attempts but does not verify that the multipart payload is intact on the retry."]}
